title: Context-aware request slicing + speculative kernel warmup for embedding tail reduction
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Investigate and implement a two-pronged approach to reduce p95/p99 latency for the embeddings endpoint serving reranking workloads: 1) context-aware request slicing to avoid oversized microbatches from long-sequence tenants and 2) speculative kernel warmup + lightweight prefetch to reduce first-kernel tail spikes. Goal: reduce p99 by >=20% and p95 by >=15% on the heavy tail without regressions to throughput or quality.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for reranking embedding endpoint reduced by >=20% on synthetic heavy-tail workload (95th percentile of tenants)
p95 improved by >=15% with no regression in avg throughput >5%
no measurable drop in embedding cosine similarity (mean <0.5% change) on regression tests
can be toggled via runtime flags per-tenant for staged rollout
comments: 2026-02-10 — Arjun: Kickoff. Collected baseline traces for reranking traffic (tenant sample A/B). Baseline p99 = 512ms, p95 = 188ms, p50 = 22ms. Observed two dominant tail modes: (a) oversized requests that force long microbatch cycles, (b) cold kernel specialization on large-seq kernels causing 120–200ms spikes.

2026-02-11 — Marina: Prototypeed request slicer that splits requests above N tokens into sliding windows to keep microbatch variance low. Chose conservative default slice_size=768 and overlap=64 to preserve contextual quality for reranking prompts.

2026-02-12 — Eng experiment #1: Enabled slicer in staging for 20% of traffic. Result: p95 down from 188ms to 165ms (-12%), p99 down to 430ms (-16%). Throughput dropped ~2.3% on heavy workloads due to extra forward passes; embedding similarity regression on rerank tests = +0.2% mean difference (within tolerance).

2026-02-13 — Eng experiment #2: Implemented speculative kernel warmup that launches a lightweight prefill for the most-likely kernel variant when a large request arrives; warmup uses a short KV prefix to prime caches. Staging traffic (20%): observed reduction of cold-kernel spikes by ~85% for spikes attributable to kernel specialization—p99 further reduced to 360ms.

2026-02-14 — PM review: Agreed to combine both techniques behind per-tenant flags with telemetry. Need rollout gating and additional safety checks for memory pressure and GPU kernel queue backpressure.

2026-02-15 — Design feedback (Nora Lee): Ensure slicing semantics are documented in API contract for private deployments; recommend adding optional header to signal 'preserve-boundaries' for customers who must avoid slicing.

2026-02-16 — Infra note (Samir Gupta): Verified that speculative warmup increases short-lived CUDA allocations; added soft cap to number of concurrent speculative warmups per-GPU to avoid OOM scenarios. Also added metric speculative_warmup_rejected_count.

2026-02-17 — Current status: Combined rollout in staging with 50% traffic. Aggregate staging numbers: p50 20ms, p95 154ms, p99 312ms. Estimated net p99 improvement vs baseline = 39%. Proceeding to safety/perf runbook and limited production canary for three tenants with heavy reranking traffic next week.

Next steps: (a) Add A/B dashboard for similarity quality metrics (cosine distribution), (b) Implement per-tenant opt-out header and runtime toggle, (c) Create rollback playbook and automated memory pressure guardrails, (d) Finalize PR review and QA.
decision_log: Decision 2026-02-11: Use sliding-window slicing (overlap=64) to trade minimal quality delta for large latency wins on oversized requests.
Decision 2026-02-13: Implement speculative warmup instead of synchronous kernel precompilation to minimize synchronous blocking; cap concurrent warmups per GPU.
Decision 2026-02-16: Rollout via per-tenant feature flags with telemetry gating; default OFF for dedicated/private customers until documented.
Rejected alternative: Shard-level aggressive batching (rejected due to large throughput regression and complexity with tenant fairness).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Slicing could change embedding vectors for some prompts leading to rerank quality regressions. Mitigation: run offline quality regression suite and keep slice overlap; provide per-tenant opt-out.
Risk: Speculative warmup increases transient memory pressure. Mitigation: soft caps, backoff, and reject counters; track OOMs in SLO alerting.
Risk: Combined change might increase token throughput cost. Mitigation: measure cost delta in canary; consider dynamic enablement only for tenants in heavy-tail cohort.
